🗒️What This Means For You
  • Fed Hike: Since the 2026-09-16 Fed hike the Treasury-rate leg of IG returns is +0.70% (intraday, 7-year -10bp). At trading day 33 (last close) it was +1.07% against a five-campaign average of -1.15% at the same point — 1994-95, 1999-00, 2022-23 were worse. The spread leg adds -1.05%. The 10-year is -6bp since the hike vs a +16bp campaign average at the same point. The 2s10s steepening may be topping (intraday 3 of 4 signals: topping likely).
  • HY Contagion: Junk-bond stress: the CCC-to-single-B spread gap is 780bp against a five-year average of 417bp (widest since Apr 2020). Better-rated junk is following: single-B +36bp and BB +20bp in a month. CCC and single-B are moving together more (correlation 0.41 → 0.65 over 3 months; five-year norm 0.69). Investment grade is moving too (+10bp in a month).
  • AI Credit: CoreWeave 5Y CDS 1,153bp, +44bp since 2026-11-02, 41bp under the Oct 15 record and 701bp over the June low. Its June 9.625% 2032s are at 79.9 (15.0%, -5.5pts in a month). Up the stack: Nvidia 146bp, Oracle 307bp. Neocloud stocks 1m: CRWV -44%, NBIS -42%, IREN -47% vs NVDA -14%.
  • Tech Phase: Phase 1 of the 2000 template, day 20 after the tech basket's 2026-10-06 peak: basket -15.7% vs -17.1% for 2000 on the same day. Model odds of being in spread widening or worse: 42% in 3m, 40% in 6m; odds spreads cross the Phase-2 line at some point within 12m: 61%. 6m odds +8.9pp since 2026-11-02. Triggered signposts: Basket names >20% off high.

A split, rate-heavy session. The Nasdaq Composite gained +0.825175% to 25372.01 and the S&P 500 +0.364919% to 7568.92, both helped by a +1.31% bounce in US Info Tech. The Dow fell -0.3794631%, and Europe was weaker: STOXX 600 -0.5820399%, FTSE 100 -1.142052%. Long yields drove the day. The US 10Y rose 4.96bp to 4.9621%, the 30Y reached 5.3265%, and the Gilt 10Y jumped 6.9bp to 5.261%. The VIX eased to 20.83 from 21.15, so sentiment is better than last session but not calm. The biggest story is under the surface, in junk credit. Headline HY OAS is benign at 3.39 (z-score -0.6, 26th percentile), but the hy_contagion read shows the Caa-B gap at 780bp. That is its 99.5th percentile over five years and the widest since 2020-04-16, against a 5y average of about 417bp. Is the CCC stress spreading? Partly. Single-B OAS widened 36bp over the month, Ba widened 20bp and the IG index widened 10bp. The 63-day Caa/B correlation of daily changes has climbed from 0.41 three months ago to 0.65 now, approaching its 0.69 5y median. That is consistent with stress starting to travel up the quality ladder, not yet a broad repricing. This is a descriptive read, not a validated signal. The AI credit stack points the same way. CoreWeave 5Y CDS rose 43.8bp on the day to about 1153bp. That is about 41bp below its 1,194.5bp Oct 15 record, and it has now retraced 94.5% of the run from the 452bp June low. Nvidia's own CDS slipped 1.79bp to 145.65bp. So far the market is pricing neocloud risk without passing it on to the guarantor. Read descriptively, the market is not fully buying the backstop for CoreWeave itself, but it is not doubting Nvidia either. The tech phase model keeps today's basket in Phase 1 (initial drop, credit calm), 20 days past the peak. One signpost has triggered: 57.1% of basket names are more than 20% off their highs, against a 50% line. The model's 6-month odds of Phase 2 or Phase 3 rose 8.9pp versus the prior session. The phase model now puts a 45.4% chance on ever reaching Phase 2+ within 3 months and 60.6% within 12 months (model estimates). The relief-rally watch is armed but not confirmed: VIX has spiked while credit stays calm, and the turn needs VIX at or below 19.0.

NY Harbor ULSD (US Diesel) — current: 453.06 cents/gal vs WTI

NY Harbor ULSD is at 453.06 cents/gal, an extreme reading at the 99.5th percentile with a z-score of 2.96. Two-sided analog episodes per signal: days where the signal's percentile-rank (vs its own full history) was <=5th or >=95th, or |z-score|>=1.3, clustered into one episode per zone per >=6-month gap between episode starts. For each zone, the realized forward 6-month % change in the BENCHMARK'S OUTRIGHT PRICE from each episode start is measured; a card's direction (BUY/SELL) is whichever sign that median historical move carries. Entry/target/stretch/stop are computed directly from this table -- the narrative prose (thesis/rationale) is the only part supplied by an LLM, and it is not permitted to alter a number. Crack spreads and curve shapes are, financially, relative-value signals rather than clean predictors of outright price; expressing every card in outright price terms is a deliberate simplification. HO36 Comdty (ULSD's 36-month point) is thin/less liquid on this seat -- treat its curve-shape reading with lower confidence than the others. Not investment advice.

Churn = the longest window of 20-120 sessions whose close range is <= 8x its median ATR(14), with median ADX(14) < 20, an insignificant close-price slope (p > 0.05), and >= 2 entries into each edge zone (top/bottom 20% of the band). Support/resistance = median swing low/high (+/-5 sessions); outer edges = the window's extreme closes. Breakout = a close beyond the outer edge by > 0.5 ATR, confirmed by a second close or one close beyond 1 ATR. A break back inside within 5 sessions is a failed break. An episode's outer edges can widen at most 0.5 ATR past their first detection, so a slow grind can't drag the range along with it. Base rates come from replaying the same rules over the full history, day by day, with no lookahead. This is pattern analysis of historical prices, not investment advice.

💧Treasury liquidity & rates volcomputed

US Govt Securities Liquidity Index (GVLQUSD), MOVE, Fed DKW term premium and TLT option skew, live from Bloomberg + federalreserve.gov.

Five charts tracking the mechanism Simon White laid out for why Treasury liquidity is deteriorating: rising inflation volatility feeds into a higher term premium, which steepens the curve, which raises bond vol, which shows up as worse UST market liquidity. Right now UST liquidity is at the 50th percentile of its own history (higher = worse) and the Fed's own DKW real term premium is +91bp.

Latest reading is +0.41 vol points (5th percentile of the 59 runs recorded so far). Positive means the 5%-OTM put is pricier than the at-the-money option -- the market paying up for downside-price / higher-yield insurance on long-end Treasuries.

UST liquidity index is 1.53 (50th percentile of its own 2007-present history -- 100th = worst liquidity on record), improving over the past 3 months (-0.08 pts). CPI YoY volatility (2yr) is 0.50pp; the article's thesis is that rising inflation vol drags liquidity worse, which this chart is built to let you check month to month.

Real term premium is +91bp (96th percentile of its own 2007-present history), up 12bp over the trailing ~2 months. Inflation risk premium is +14bp. Fed staff's own DKW decomposition (D'Amico-Kim-Wei, updated Kim-Walsh-Wei) splits the rise in long yields into a policy-uncertainty component (real term premium) and an inflation-uncertainty component -- both rising is the article's read that this move isn't just a rate-expectations story.

MOVE is 100.0 (72th percentile of its own post-2007 history). The 3m10s curve is 83bp (steeper by 4bp over 3 months). The article's claim is mechanical, not just correlated -- a steeper curve gives forward rates more room to move before converging to spot, which is itself higher realized/implied vol.

MOVE and the UST liquidity index have moved together with a full-history correlation of +0.72 (both series read as 'worse' when they rise). That's the closing link in the article's chain: inflation vol -> term premium -> curve steepness -> bond vol -> liquidity.

Term premium is the Fed's own DKW model series (D'Amico-Kim-Wei, updated Kim-Walsh-Wei), pulled directly from federalreserve.gov, not Bloomberg. Not a trading signal -- a liquidity/vol monitor only.

Same test on each trailing window: cup base = lowest close in the window, left rim = highest close before it, right rim = highest close after it. Cup complete at ≥90% retracement; above 110% the yield has run past the old high (a breakout, not a cup). No cup inside the window when its left rim is not the highest close of the 91 days before it, i.e. yields were already falling into the window. Pass level = cup base + 0.90 × (left rim − cup base).

🗞️Street View — Where the Cycle Is HeadingCURATED · AS OF 2026-10-01

⚠ Commentary is 33 days old (as of 2026-10-01); it may not reflect the latest Fed news.

Consensus is a short, shallow campaign: one or two more 25bp hikes, December more likely than October. The debate is whether hiking into an energy shock ends in recession, and the bond market is already doing some of the tightening.

The Fed

  • Sept 16: unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00%, the first since 2023. Dots: median one more hike in 2026; 16 of 18 see at least one, 4 see two. Inflation not back at 2% until 2029. (CNBC, FedAndMarkets)
  • Warsh's message was distinctly hawkish (inflation 'too high and broad-based'); the Conference Board calls it 'not a one and done'. (Conference Board)
  • Sept 29, Williams (NY Fed): 'no need for urgency'; one more hike 'late this year' may be appropriate; the biggest inflation shocks have passed. (Bloomberg, NY Fed)
  • Sept 30, August PCE came in soft: headline 3.4% (vs 3.7% expected), core 3.0% (vs 3.3%). October odds fell; December still priced. Kashkari: inflation 'still too high'. (CNBC, CNBC (Kashkari))

Market pricing

  • October 28 hike odds vary widely by venue, roughly 35% to 69% (prediction markets highest, CME futures ~58%), mostly measured before the soft PCE print. (PredictionMarketsPicks)
  • About 83% odds of another hike by year-end; futures price ~93bp of tightening over the next 9 meetings, more than the dots. (Forbes)

Bonds and credit

  • 10-year Treasury above 5.25% (Sept 28), the highest since 2007; 30-year ~5.49%. Drivers cited: sticky energy inflation (Iran war), heavy issuance, AI capex demand. Term premium ~1.0–1.4%. (CNBC, CNBC (Warsh's yield problem))
  • AI-related issuers trade ~115bp vs ~78bp for IG overall; high-yield AI supply $40B year to date vs $12B in all of 2025. BNP and Goldman warn the issuance could pressure spreads. (Reuters, Bloomberg (BNP))

The bear case

  • Rosenberg: the Fed has never hiked into an energy shock without a recession, and AI won't save it this time. (TheStreet)
  • Goldman called the case for hiking 'weak' (demand not overheating, energy inflation should fade when the war ends). Oxford Economics: 'The Fed cannot control energy prices'; the risk is a weaker labor market. (CNN)

Read-through: For bonds, the bigger risk is the long end, not the Fed: term premium and supply keeping the 10-year above 5% matter more than one extra 25bp. The recession call is loud but isn't in any sell-side house view yet.

Curated summary of published Fed, market and economist commentary (news and research via the web), not a computed series and not a forecast. Odds differ by venue and move daily.

🔥Is Inflation Persistent?

Persistence score: 60/100 — Sticky but not re-accelerating at the core. Underlying measures are clustered at 2.26-2.82% and mostly flat. Median CPI is 2.61 and falling, trimmed-mean CPI 2.66, median PCE 2.67, and core sticky CPI 2.78. All sit around the middle-to-upper part of their historical ranges (computed Core-Trend Sub-Score shown separately). The pressure is at the edges. Flexible CPI is 6.12% and rising (82nd percentile), consistent with an energy shock. Dallas Fed breadth shows 26.8% of the PCE basket rising faster than 5% (16.6% above 10% plus 10.2% at 5-10%), while 25.6% is falling, a bimodal distribution. Headline core PCE at 3.12 runs above core CPI at 2.6. Persistence is real enough that the Fed cannot cut, but there is no wage spiral: AHE 3.0, ECI 0.8.

🫧Tech Bubble Peak Again?vs March 2000
BUBBLE RESEMBLANCE · SUPER COUNT computed
9 of 22 indicators at peak-like levels · 7 beyond 2000 — 59/100
Today looks less like March 2000 and more like the months after it. On the computed indicators, Equity Froth is far from the 2000 peak: Nasdaq trailing P/E is 39.58x against 175x (15% of the way there), stretch above the 200DMA is 1.2% against 50% (2%), and SOX P/E is 36.6x (42%). Late-cycle catalysts are mixed. Credit tightness exceeds 2000 levels (IG 123%, Baa-10Y 155%), financial conditions are looser (NFCI 152%) and VIX complacency reads 133%, but the curve at +33.12bp is not inverted and ISM PMIs show no rollover (1% and 10%). The tech phase model places the basket in Phase 1 (initial drop, credit calm), 20 days past the peak. The basket is down 15.69%, versus 17.14% for the 2000 basket on the same day. The model's 6-month odds are 49.3% P1, 29% P2, 10.9% P3 and 10.7% P4, with a 60.6% chance of ever reaching Phase 2+ within 12 months (model estimates). The breadth signpost has triggered, and SOX at -27.57% is 2.43pp from its -30% line.

Bubble-analog — today's Nasdaq vs the dot-com cycle (two anchors)

WHY TWO START DATES?
Each line is rebased to 100 at a low the tech bull launched from, so elapsed time lines up. Oct-2022 is today's anchor — it was the prior bear-market bottom. Oct-1990 is the dot-com cycle's equivalent (its literal prior bear bottom). But 1990 predates the internet mania by ~4 years, so the second chart re-anchors the dot-com line to the 1994 reset low, just before the surge ignited, for a tighter like-for-like. Today sits very early under the strict 1990 analog, further along under the 1994 surge analog.
━ Anchored at the prior bear-market bottom (Oct-1990)   ━ today's cycle
━ Anchored at the pre-internet reset low (1994)   ━ today's cycle

Valuation marker: today's Nasdaq P/E (40x) ≈ 23% of the ~175x 2000-peak P/E.

IF THIS RHYMES WITH 2000
Nasdaq fell -78.0% peak→trough (2000-03-10 → 2002-10-09, ~31 months); it took ~15 years to reclaim the high.

The bubble debate has moved from 'are we at the top?' to 'how does the unwind travel?'. Valuations were never near dot-com extremes, but the drawdown is behaving like early 2001: leadership is breaking (Comm Services -15.29% and Info Tech -10.42% over 1m), while credit and macro stay benign. The handoff the model watches for is Phase 1 to Phase 2, when credit stops being calm. The early pieces are visible in the CCC tail and in CoreWeave CDS, but not yet in headline HY at 339bp against the 448bp trigger, or in Baa-10Y. The relief-rally watch is armed: VIX has spiked while credit stays calm, and the turn needs VIX at or below 19.0. History splits almost evenly between trap rallies (48.6% trap rate, about 17.5 days, +10.7%) and real ones (about 86 days, +31.3%). The concentration, IPO-froth, CAPE, market-cap/GDP and EPS-growth figures are analyst estimates from general knowledge, not verified by search in this run.

Odds the volatility-washout conditions line up within a week: 52%; within two weeks: 60%. Rallies of 8%+ that start in this phase: 49% later fail below their starting low (median 18 trading days, +11%); the rest become recoveries (median 86 days, +31%). Descriptive, not a signal.

Positioning tilt (generic, historical): Historically, at this phase mix the phase-conditional optimum has favoured gold, Treasury duration and investment-grade credit, over mega-cap growth, developed international and emerging markets.

Phases are rules with the same thresholds in 2000 and today: Phase 2 = HY OAS +150bp or Baa-10y +50bp from the basket's peak; Phase 3 = Sahm rule or ISM < 47 for 3 months AND bank stress (KBW -25% or C&I charge-offs >= 1% and rising); Phase 4 = basket +20% off its low, above its 200-day average, HY 150bp off its wide. Odds come from every Nasdaq-100 drop since 1985 that reached today's depth, weighted by how closely its credit, macro and volatility readings matched today's, plus a small labelled judgment overlay for AI-credit stress. 'Ever P2+' = chance spreads cross the Phase-2 line at any point before the horizon. Model estimates on ~40 episodes: read them to within +/-10 points. Not financial advice.

🏦Fed Chair Warsh
NEAR TERM

Inference: a hold at the next meeting, with a hawkish tilt and no forward guidance. Warsh has said he does not want to signal whether the Fed will hike, cut or hold. At Sintra he reaffirmed the 2% target, rejected the case for cuts and did not rule out hikes. With core PCE at 3.12 and the 10Y near 5%, nothing in his record argues for a cut.

~1 YEAR

Inference: policy rates flat to modestly higher, plus an active push to shrink and restructure the balance sheet and overhaul Fed operations, as he signaled at his April Senate hearing and on taking office. June projections showed nine officials expecting at least one hike in 2026. A hike becomes more likely if flexible-price inflation passes into core.

Sourced record: at Warsh's first meeting as chair in June, the Fed held at 3.5-3.75% unanimously, and the new dots leaned toward hikes. Warsh submitted no dot of his own (PBS, ClickOrlando/AP). Fortune described his debut press conference as less 'regime change' and more 'we'll see'. His Senate hearing emphasized the balance sheet and inflation (Fortune, Apr 21), and he has sought an operational overhaul (The National). We could not verify any FOMC decisions or Warsh remarks after late July 2026, including Jackson Hole, so the current policy rate and his latest stance are n/a. Both estimates above are inferences from his prior record.

Sources: PBS NewsHour - What Warsh's first meeting as Fed chair signals · Fortune - How did the market react to Kevin Warsh's press conference · Fortune - Warsh-era Fed balance sheet, inflation: Senate hearing · The National - Kevin Warsh seeks overhaul of Federal Reserve operations · TMGM - What did Kevin Warsh say in his first international appearance? · ClickOrlando/AP - All eyes turn to Fed chair Kevin Warsh

Descriptive regime read, not advice and not a recommendation to trade. Rule results are simulations on one market history (3x daily returns rebuilt from index data, 1-day lag, costs), and the exits (+10% target, 5-day pause) were chosen after testing a few values on that same history, so treat them as in-sample. The trend+vol engine is a drawdown control, not proven timing skill (trendvol TRENDVOL.md § CORRECTION). Credit widening = 63-day change past the monitor_spread triggers (Baa +0.15pp, HY OAS +0.50pp, IG OAS +0.15pp); as a standalone overlay that rule failed its pre-registered gates. Leveraged and inverse ETFs reset daily and decay.
